title: What a Drop Reveals: Sim-to-Real Material Estimation for Deformable Objects from Video
abstract: arXiv:2611.34894v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How an object deforms when it hits the ground reveals what it is made of. From a single real video of a drop, we estimate a deformable object's density-normalized stiffness $E/\rho$, and its yield stress $\sigma_Y/\rho$ when the impact causes plastic deformation, with a feed-forward predictor trained only in simulation. Real videos carry no material labels, so such predictors are developed and validated on synthetic data alone. We show that synthetic validation ranks their geometric inputs in the wrong order. Material acts through 3D deformation, and tracklets lifted to 3D with estimated depth are indeed the most accurate input in simulation. However, on real drops they are the least accurate, and better depth does not repair them: the failure persists with simulator depth in training, LiDAR depth at test time, and exact depth on rendered replays of the real drops. Short 2D optical-flow tracklets do the opposite: they improve nothing i

translated_title: 一次坠落揭示了什么：从视频实现可变形物体材料属性的模拟到真实（Sim-to-Real）估计
translated_abstract: 一个物体落地时如何形变，揭示了它的材质构成。仅需一段真实的坠落视频，我们即可估计可变形物体的密度归一化刚度 E/ρ，以及在冲击引起塑性变形时的屈服应力 σY/ρ，所用的前馈预测器仅在仿真中训练。由于真实视频不含材料标签，这类预测器只能在合成数据上进行开发与验证。我们证明，合成数据的验证会把几何输入的优劣排出错误的顺序。材料属性通过三维形变起作用，因此借助估计深度提升到三维的轨迹在仿真中确实是最准确的输入；然而在真实坠落中它们却最不准确，而且更好的深度也无法修复这一问题：无论训练时使用仿真深度、测试时使用LiDAR深度，还是在真实坠落的渲染回放中使用精确深度，这种失败都持续存在。而短的二维光流轨迹恰恰相反：它们在仿真中毫无改进……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 本论文发现仅用合成数据验证会误导输入表示的选择——仿真中最准确的三维轨迹输入在真实坠落视频上反而最差、且无法靠更好的深度修复，而简单的二维光流短轨迹在真实场景中最有效，从而实现了仅凭仿真训练、从单段真实坠落视频估计可变形物体刚度与屈服应力的sim-to-real方法。
en_tdlr: This work shows that synthetic-only validation ranks input representations incorrectly—3D tracklets that excel in simulation fail on real drop videos regardless of depth quality, while short 2D optical-flow tracklets generalize best—enabling a purely simulation-trained predictor to estimate deformable objects' stiffness and yield stress from a single real drop video.
